author: ValWood
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**


GO:0010629 | negative regulation of gene expression | IEA with ARBA00026647



* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC1347.07 
https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC637.09  (and orthologs in other species)


* **Description of issue**

This is an endonuclease involved in 3' end processing so unlikely to be a regulator of a process.


This seems to come from a single C. elegans annotation:
https://www.alliancegenome.org/gene/WB:WBGene00004095
title: GO:0010629	 negative regulation of gene expression IEA with ARBA00026647

author: claude[bot]
source_title: Critical review of ARBA00026647: Recommend immediate deprecation of overly complex gene expression regulation mega-rule

author: Antonialock
body: There were two experimental masters for this ARBA annotation to proteins matching funfam 3.30.420.10:FF:000031 from worm Q10124 PQE1_CAEEL (uniprot annotation, I removed it. the paper called it a phenotype with unknow mechanism) the other is an SGD annotation for Q12090 REX3 which is annotated to "regulatory ncRNA 3'-end processing" This term has the parent "negative regulation of gene expression", should this relationship exist?

author: ValWood
body: It does look a bit weird. @pgaudet  thoughts?

author: Antonialock
body:
There are regulatory ncRNAs that positively regulate gene expression eg enhancer RNAs
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhancer_RNA

author: pgaudet
body:
We had decided that the ncRNA processing was part of the regulation of gene expression, see 
https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/23081

I am pretty sure that @hattrill said this should be part_of and not upstream, but I'll let her confirm.

author: ValWood
body: In this case should it be just "regulation"  not "negative regulation"

author: hattrill
body:
The processing aspect was something I didn't really have anything to do with. 

Personally, I have never liked that ncRNA processing is part of the gene silencing - to me it's like saying that mRNA processing is part every other pathway involving a protein. But, I left it on the 'pick your battles' pile!

Would be really happy to revisit this and make some systematic changes.
